summary: Learn business architecture for digital transformation with capability maps, value streams, and roadmaps. Train your team to align strategy and delivery.
lede: Business Architecture for Digital Transformation helps you translate strategy into capability, value stream, information, and governance decisions that guide change. You will learn to map capabilities, analyse value streams and gaps, prioritise roadmaps, and connect investment choices to business outcomes using approaches such as TOGAF and the Business Model Canvas. Through guided exercises, you will practise stakeholder mapping, architecture heat mapping, roadmap sequencing, and preparation of an executive-ready business architecture pack. The course helps you align strategy, account for legacy systems, budget pressure, competing priorities, and uneven data quality, then communicate a defensible plan to delivery teams and senior leaders.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who need to connect strategy, capability design, and transformation delivery in complex organizations. Enterprise Architects who govern capability maps and transition states. Business Architects who define capability models and value streams. Transformation Managers who prioritize change portfolios and roadmaps. Strategy Managers who align operating models to digital initiatives. Product Owners who translate business needs into delivery backlogs. Enterprise Governance Leads who review architecture decisions and controls. Process Improvement Analysts who link process gaps to capabilities. Data Governance Managers who map information dependencies across change. PMO Leads who sequence initiatives against business value. Digital Transformation Consultants who prepare executive architecture packs.
prerequisites: Recommended preparation includes a working understanding of business strategy, operating models, process maps, or enterprise transformation projects. No coding is required, but you should be comfortable reading capability maps, simple portfolio data, and stakeholder-based decision documents. Prior exposure to TOGAF, business process management, or enterprise architecture is helpful but not mandatory.
